title: Plural -S Endings
subtitle: /s/, /z/, and /ɪz/
description: The -S ending for plurals and third-person verbs has three distinct pronunciations. Mastering them gives your English a polished, natural rhythm.
tip: After hissing sounds (s, z, sh, ch, j) say /ɪz/; after other voiced sounds say /z/; after other voiceless sounds say /s/.
phrases: James watches movies, fixes computers, and washes dishes every weekend.
Cats and dogs are common pets, but foxes and wolves are not.
She runs five miles, lifts weights, and stretches before breakfast.
The buses stop at the benches near the churches and bridges.
He reads books, solves puzzles, and teaches classes on weekdays.
Birds, bees, and butterflies fill the gardens in spring.
